notes:
PASS on the fake backend; the gate exits 0 and the evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached or run and no human review or test is claimed. The card has no entry_symbols; its models[0], mjpc/tasks/fingers/task.xml, is confirmed and served as a configuration-only MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0 (device mhs://localhost/mujoco-mpc-fingers, kind world.sim). cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [6]}}; the bridge derives each ctrl interval from the model's actuator_ctrlrange, which the six intvelocity actuators set to -.99..99 at task.xml:93-100, and refuses an out-of-range element with MHS.SAFETY.ENVELOPE_VIOLATION before writing data.ctrl. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The world state is the bridge's time_ms/qpos/qvel/ctrl/tick/timestep_ms/seed; the model's timestep is 0.001 s (task.xml:4), so timestep_ms is 1.0. The model file and its ../common.xml include (task.xml:2) are read in place from the read-only clone at the pinned commit; neither the model nor any upstream code is copied, imported, installed or modified. MuJoCo is not installed or importable where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module (fake.py, backend .fake:fake_mujoco): it parses the MJCF and its include graph for the actuator count, the per-actuator control ranges, the qpos/qvel dimensions and the timestep, but its integration is a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated slide joint toward its control target. It resolves no contact, friction, inertia, equality, tendon, actuator or sensor dynamics, and it does not integrate the two free bodies (object and target) or load meshes/textures. MuJoCo was never imported, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine; a backend that resolves the real mujoco module (sim) was not run here. Expected simulator-family warnings, all explained in facts.md and none failing: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library rather than a package class the gate can record and compare, and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived ticks, action.ctrl and reset seed inputs. G4 reported no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warning: every Fact cites a text line of README.md, docs/OVERVIEW.md, mjpc/tasks/tasks.cc, mjpc/tasks/fingers/fingers.cc or mjpc/tasks/fingers/task.xml. The package declares no Limit of its own and no operator-required bound; the ctrl envelope is derived from the model. NOT COVERED: the MuJoCo engine and every trajectory-level behaviour; the MJPC C++ task layer (the Fingers residual at fingers.cc:34-54, the task settings at task.xml:7-18, the planners and the GUI); the home keyframe at task.xml:20-34, because the bridge's reset applies mj_resetData rather than a keyframe; rendering, cameras and images; the other MJPC tasks and models in the clone; snapshot/restore beyond the bridge's fallback time/qpos/qvel/act/ctrl copy (the stand-in has no mj_getState/mj_setState); and any physical hardware. test_driver.py keeps the check_driver call and adds six cases (model shape from the card model, per-actuator ctrl-range refusals with no state change, state following the control target, reset, published fidelity contract and the e-stop latch); they pass on the fake backend. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only the catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1.
